epistemic_purpose: repair stale live Backgrounded + Cancel projection after authoritative CommandJob terminality

verdict_history.summary: Multi-job production projection bug: the runner fired onBackgroundStateChange(false, undefined) ONLY on the >0->0 cardinal flip. When J1 terminalized while J2 stayed running, no callback fired; J1's projection stayed 'running' forever (stale Backgrounded pill). The predecessor's BCTCP-06 multi-job test manually injected the desired end state but did NOT exercise the production composition.

Bounded repair moves the per-job terminal signal UPSTREAM to the runner (carrying jobId + terminalState, NOT gated on becameIdle). Controller projection maintains the per-job map, derives the scalar from it, and computes the active taskId as the LAST running entry. BTCONT predicate fires exactly once on the >0->0 transition. Controller-only proxy test BCTCP-CTL-MULTI-01..05 proves the controller seam but only ASSUMES the runner emits the right tuple.

Adds BCTCP-RUNNER-MULTI-01..04 at the EXACT production seam: real createVscodeRunCommandsTool + real createVscodeShellExecutor + real CommandJobManager.start. The RED was captured against predecessor e588d0541 (BCTCP-RUNNER-MULTI-01 returned 'Received: []' because the predecessor's `if (becameIdle)` gate dropped J1's signal entirely; BCTCP-RUNNER-MULTI-02 returned only the cardinal [false, undefined, undefined] tuple). The four tests now PASS GREEN against correction01, proving the runner-composition closure of the multi-job false-green.

reproduction_red_001.post_correction01_runner_seam_behavior: Runner fires (false, J1, 'cancelled') UNCONDITIONALLY via `start.terminalPromise.then(({jobId, terminalState}) => notify(false, jobId, terminalState))`; BCTCP-RUNNER-MULTI-01 GREEN (spy's per-job tuple contains J1's exact jobId+terminalState)
